title: The Crown of Ironhollow
premise: Lior Blackwood has spent ten years guarding the sealed gate of Ironhollow, the last door into the buried kingdom of Vael, until a starving child named Sef arrives speaking Old Vaelish and bearing a birthmark that marks them as the lost heir. When the usurper Malrec's inquisitors burn the mountain villages hunting the child, Lior must choose between the safe anonymity of gatekeeping and carrying Sef through smuggler roads to the free cities, where the child's blood could either crown a rightful ruler or reopen the war that buried Vael. Along the way Lior learns their own family sealed the gate not to protect the world from Vael, but to hide what they did to its last king. In the end, Lior chooses neither throne nor silence: they unseal the gate on their own terms, offering Vael's survivors a homeland rather than a conquest, and pay for it by surrendering the only thing they ever truly owned—the key, and with it their belonging anywhere at all.
about_author: Jonah Nakamura is a former trail-crew foreman who writes fantasy shaped by years of walking abandoned mining roads through the Cascades. They live in a converted fire lookout with two dogs and an unreasonable number of maps.

chapters.title: The Gatekeeper's Winter
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A quiet opening establishes Ironhollow's routines: checking seals, trading with smugglers, keeping ledgers no one reads. Lior is competent but hollow, defined by duty inherited from a father who never explained why. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment, just before it breaks.

chapters.title: A Knock in Dead Language
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. During a blizzard, a child—Sef—collapses at the gatehouse, raving in a tongue Lior's ledger books identify as Old Vaelish, dead for three centuries. The child bears a mark like a broken crown. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as Lior realizes the seal hums when the child cries.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Omit
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with flashbacks. Searching ancestral records for the birthmark, Lior finds pages razored out across generations—a deliberate erasure. The first inquisitor outriders appear in the valley below. Emotional beat: the discovery that inheritance can be a wound, not a gift.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. The child remembers the burned village of Thornfell, the gray-cloaked riders, and a dying woman pressing a copper token into small hands. Emotional beat: grief rendered as survival instinct; Sef trusts no one, least of all the tall keeper with sad eyes.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior bargains with Ferro Askan, a smuggler queen who owes Lior a debt and collects secrets as interest. She recognizes the mark instantly—and names her price for passage: the truth of what's behind the gate. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; every ally costs something.

chapters.title: Riders in Gray
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Inquisitor Captain Vess Corhane arrives at Ironhollow under polite pretense, probing Lior's loyalty while her soldiers search the passes. Lior hides Sef in the old cisterns, nearly discovered. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Lior discovers they can lie well, and hates it.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: Lior and Sef's alternating POV. Flight begins through smuggler tunnels beneath Thornfell. Sef's language instincts unlock old wardstones, opening ways no living person should know. Emotional beat: first fragile bond—Lior teaching survival, Sef teaching wonder.

chapters.title: The Free City of Marrowgate
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The pair reaches Marrowgate's refugee sprawl, where exiled Vaeli descendants still whisper prayers in half-remembered Old Vaelish. Sef is recognized; crowds kneel. Emotional beat: belonging offered too fast—adoration that feels like being devoured.

chapters.title: Council of Ashes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The exile council splits: crown the child and march on Malrec, or kill the heir to keep the war buried. Lior realizes both factions see Sef as a tool, not a child. Emotional beat: disillusionment; freedom's defenders can be as ruthless as usurpers.

chapters.title: The Copper Token
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef reveals the token's secret—it's a key-half, and it sings near Lior's gate-ledger sigil. The Blackwoods didn't guard the gate; they held the other half. Emotional beat: betrayal blooming slowly; Sef wonders if kindness was always custody.

chapters.title: Blood and Ledger Ink
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Confronting the erased records' final surviving page, hidden in a Marrowgate scriptorium, Lior learns the truth: Aldric Blackwood betrayed the last king of Vael, sealing the gates on a fleeing people to buy his family's place in the new order. Emotional beat: shame as inheritance; Lior vomits, then goes very calm.

chapters.title: Corhane's Mercy
chapters.summary: Vess Corhane's POV. The inquisitor captain, hunting them, is revealed as more than a zealot—she carries orders to bring the heir alive because Malrec needs royal blood for a ritual to permanently bind the gate shut forever, entombing anyone left inside. Emotional beat: enemy humanized; she believes she is saving lives.

chapters.title: Night of Knives
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The council's hardline faction attempts to seize Sef and force an early coronation; assassins come in the dark. Lior and an unlikely ally—Corhane, who refuses entombment—fight their way out of Marrowgate with Sef. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice, and the shock of fighting beside your hunter.

chapters.title: The Long Descent
chapters.summary: Lior, Sef, and Corhane's rotating POV. Fugitives now to everyone, they cross the high passes toward Ironhollow, pursued by both armies. Starvation, avalanche, and grudging trust. Sef asks Lior if home is a place or a promise. Emotional beat: found-family forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Malrec Unmasked
chapters.summary: Corhane's POV. Intercepted dispatches reveal Malrec's true design: he isn't Vaeli or free-city born—he's the descendant of the exiles' own betrayer, and the ritual will make him immortal warden of a kingdom-sized tomb. Emotional beat: horror reframing the whole war; everyone has been fighting over a grave.

chapters.title: Ironhollow Besieged
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They reach the gate to find Malrec's vanguard already digging at the seals. Ferro Askan's smugglers arrive—not to save Lior, but because Lior paid their toll in advance with the ledger's trade routes. Emotional beat: debts honored coldly become salvation anyway.

chapters.title: The King Beneath the Door
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Inside the antechamber, Sef communes with the gate's deathless remnant of the last king—who does not want a throne restored, but a people freed from a three-hundred-year lie. He offers Sef the choice: crown, key, or closure. Emotional beat: awe and terrible clarity; a child asked to carry an empire's guilt.

chapters.title: Three Keys, One Choice
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Malrec arrives in person; Corhane turns her soldiers against him at cost of her own commission. In the confrontation, Lior offers the Blackwood key-half openly—refusing to let inheritance be hoarded again. Emotional beat: climax of theme; surrendering ownership as the ultimate act of belonging.

chapters.title: The Gate Stands Open
chapters.summary: Lior and Sef's shared POV. The ritual inverted, the gate opens not onto treasure or army but onto Vael's hidden survivors—thousands alive in the deep halls, sealed in by fear as much as malice. Malrec, denied his tomb, falls to his own collapsing working. Emotional beat: catharsis; the war dies of starvation instead of battle.

chapters.title: Kingdoms Without Crowns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The free cities negotiate with the emerging Vaeli nation; Sef, offered the crown, instead becomes the first Voice—an elected speaker. Corhane accepts exile rather than serve either side. Emotional beat: bittersweet politics; peace built from compromise, not victory.

chapters.title: What Lior Carried
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With the key surrendered and melted into the new treaty bell, Lior is a keeper of nothing—unemployed, unmoored, unexpectedly light. Sef asks them to stay as a citizen, not a warden. Emotional beat: grief for the old identity, and the terrifying gift of choosing your own place.

chapters.title: Spring at Ironhollow
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue. One year later: the gatehouse is a school where Old Vaelish is taught to children of both worlds. Lior still walks the wall each morning—not guarding against anything, just greeting the day. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging finally earned, not inherited.
